5.content: Prioritize ratings by immediate safety first: assign lowest ratings to moves landing on H, adjacent to visible H, or decreasing min distance to any visible H; then boost for decreasing Manhattan distance to G only if safety is maintained or improved; penalize progress that trades safety for goal proximity near hazards; prefer steady progress in safe F spaces, allowing calculated risks toward goal only if no safer progress option exists to avoid stagnation or loops; rate higher moves maintaining/increasing hazard distance in free spaces; penalize repeated moves in the same row or column without net progress toward G to prevent looping into hazards; reward moves that show clear directional progress toward G in safe paths, even if slightly longer, to encourage efficient trajectories over myopic local choices; specifically penalize persistent down-moves in the same column when they lead toward visible hazards below without lateral deviation toward G; assign lower ratings to sequences of repeated directional moves (e.g., continuous 'move_down' in the same column) that fail to reduce Manhattan distance to G or increase distance from hazards, favoring lateral or diagonal exploration to escape linear traps leading to hazards.
